description: Data scientists turn raw data into decisions. They explore datasets, build statistical and machine learning models, design experiments, and communicate findings to stakeholders through clear visualisations and written analysis.

Machine learning engineers take models from notebook to production. They build training pipelines, optimise model performance, expose models behind APIs, and own deployment, monitoring and retraining in a cloud environment.

Data analysts answer business questions with data. They write SQL against warehouses, build dashboards and reports, run statistical comparisons, and translate numbers into recommendations that non-technical teams can act on.

Backend developers build the server side of web products. They design and ship REST APIs, model relational data, handle authentication and caching, write tests, and keep services fast and reliable under load.

Frontend developers build the interfaces users touch. They turn designs into accessible, responsive components, manage client-side state, consume APIs, and tune rendering performance across browsers and devices.

Full stack developers own a feature end to end. They build the user interface, the API behind it and the database underneath, then deploy and maintain the whole thing, moving comfortably between frontend and backend work.

DevOps engineers make shipping safe and repeatable. They automate build and deployment pipelines, define infrastructure as code, containerise and orchestrate services, and run the monitoring and alerting that keeps systems healthy.

NLP engineers build systems that understand language. They preprocess text, fine-tune transformer models for classification, extraction, search and generation, evaluate quality carefully, and serve the results behind low-latency APIs.
